sections.h2: Which Wyoming office collects property tax?
sections.html:
Payments go to the City Treasurer's Office inside City Hall at 1155 28th Street SW, Wyoming, MI 49509, which also bills water, sewer and other city charges. Wyoming is in Kent County. After March 1 the Kent County Treasurer handles real property tax that is still open.

The Assessor's Office tracks about 25,000 parcels, with owner names, mailing addresses, structure photos and sketches, permit lists and transfer histories. The assessor contact shown on the Board of Review page is 616-530-7231.

Drivers can use the window behind the building, staffed Monday to Thursday from 7:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.

sections.h2: What are the Wyoming tax due dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Wyoming sets summer taxes due on August 31 and winter taxes on February 14, and its Treasurer page lists what a late payment costs.

Wyoming due dates and penalties as printed on the city Treasurer page
BillDuePenalty
SummerAugust 314% interest added September 1, then 0.5% on the first of every month, up to 6%
WinterFebruary 143% interest penalty added February 15

Unpaid real property tax is handed to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1. Business personal property tax is different: the city keeps it and adds 1% monthly until it is settled.

The summer penalty starts the day after August 31, so a closing near that date needs a title company that confirms which bill it paid.

sections.h2: What are the ways to pay Wyoming taxes?
sections.html:
Wyoming takes payment in person, by post, through a drop box and over the internet. Cash or a check brought to the Treasurer's Office adds no convenience fee.

  • Online payment runs through Invoice Cloud at wyomingmi.gov/payment. Cards carry 2.7% with a $1.95 minimum, and e-checks cost $0.80.
  • Single card payments top out at $25,000, and e-checks at $125,000.
  • Accepted online: Discover, MasterCard, American Express and Visa, plus PayPal, Venmo and e-checks.
  • For mail, write the check to the City of Wyoming and enclose the stub or account number. A drop box is at the northeast entrance of City Hall.
  • Anything received after 5:00 PM counts the next day. Never mail or drop off cash.

To learn a parcel's balance before closing, call the Treasurer's Office or follow the property information link on its page.

sections.h2: How does Wyoming value a house for tax?
sections.html:
The city assesses real property at 50% of its usual selling price, as Michigan law directs. It runs a computer assisted mass appraisal system adjusted with current market data and halves true cash value to get assessed value.

The yearly calendar is public. Value notices are mailed on the last Friday of January. Complaints go to the assessor from the first Monday in February to the second Thursday, and the roll is certified on the first Monday in March. In 2026 the assessor's review closed on February 12 and the March Board of Review closed on March 12.

The city also lists every parcel by address with its current value and last sale price, in five alphabetical street ranges, so you can compare your house with neighbors before filing.

sections.h2: How can a Wyoming owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with the assessor's review in early February. If the answer is unsatisfying, the March Board of Review is the formal venue. Its executive session falls the day after the first Monday of March, hearings open the second Monday, and every review wraps up by the first Monday of April.

  • The board may increase, decrease or confirm a value. It can also add property left off the roll and grant poverty and principal residence exemptions that were missing last year.
  • The July and December meetings fix clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact. The assessor adds qualified agricultural exemptions, taxable uncappings and poverty exemptions to that list.
  • The Michigan Tax Tribunal is the next step, with filing deadlines of May 31 for commercial and industrial property and July 31 for residential.

City Council appoints members to three year terms. Each set includes a real estate practitioner, a public accountant and a property owner who has been in the city at least a year.

sections.h2: Which other Wyoming assessing dates should an owner mark?
sections.html:
The assessor's calendar lists several dates beyond the March appeals. February 1 is the deadline for the qualified business form L-4143, and February 20 is the deadline for personal property statements (Form 632), small business property tax exemption claims (Form 5076) and the eligible manufacturing personal property affidavit (Form 5278).

  • First Monday in March: the assessor certifies the assessment roll.
  • Wednesday after the first Monday in April: the Board of Review roll goes to Kent County.
  • June 1: principal residence exemption affidavits for the summer bill.
  • November 1: the same affidavits for the winter bill.
  • December 31: tax day, which fixes the condition of a property for the next year's assessment.

Boards of Review judge a property by the facts that existed on tax day.

sections.h2: Which exemptions change when a Wyoming house is sold?
sections.html:
Under the principal residence exemption, an owner-occupied home is relieved of as much as 18 mills of school operating tax. A buyer must own and live in the home by June 1 to have it on the summer bill, or by November 1 for the winter bill, and a later move-in waits for the next tax year. The city says a form may have been signed at closing and that anyone unsure should file one with the Assessor's Office.

Only one such exemption is allowed per person, so the seller's old homestead needs a rescind form before a new one can be granted. Disabled veterans can claim a separate exemption using Form 5107 with Veterans Affairs paperwork, and the city asks for a copy of a driver's license.

A transfer affidavit is due from the buyer within 45 days, and Wyoming says missing it can bring back tax from the transfer date with penalties and interest. For an existing owner, taxable value is held down by the cap. A sale lifts it to assessed value the following year, so a new owner often sees a larger first bill.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Wyoming itself?
sections.html:
After Grand Rapids, which touches it on the northeast, Wyoming is West Michigan's second largest city. It began as a farm township organized in 1848 and incorporated as a city in 1959 after annexation fights with Grand Rapids and Grandville. The 28th Street corridor, anchored by Rogers Plaza and Studio 28, became a regional shopping strip. Growth then drifted southwest to RiverTown Crossings. General Motors shut its stamping plant in 2009, and the 74 acre site, now called Site 36, is a redevelopment focus.

Census Bureau figures: 78,588 residents in the July 2025 estimate, against 76,501 in 2020, living on 24.74 square miles of land. Among 2020 to 2024 results, 67.1% of homes are owner-occupied, owned homes have a middle value of $225,200, and rent runs $1,196 at the median. There are 29,417 households of 2.61 people each, with a median income of $73,677 and a 21.9 minute average commute.

faqs.q: What are the Wyoming, Michigan property tax deadlines?
faqs.a: August 31 for summer and February 14 for winter. Summer picks up 4% on September 1 and a half percent each month after, to a cap of 6%. Winter takes 3% on February 15.

faqs.q: Is there a place to pay Wyoming taxes without going inside City Hall?
faqs.a: Yes. A drive-up window behind City Hall is staffed Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. There is also a drop box at the northeast entrance, and online payment carries a fee.

faqs.q: Who gets a Wyoming tax bill after March 1?
faqs.a: The Kent County Treasurer collects delinquent real property tax from that date. Personal property tax stays at the city, with 1% interest each month.

faqs.q: When does a Wyoming owner dispute a value?
faqs.a: Early February for the assessor's review, then the March Board of Review, which opens hearings on the second Monday of March. Residential owners may go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by July 31.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption follow me from a Wyoming sale?
faqs.a: No. File a rescind form for the old home. The buyer applies for the exemption and qualifies by owning and occupying the house before June 1 for the summer bill or November 1 for the winter.
